title: general_name_matches: the directoryName arm and the non-DN comparison are untested
description:
## Why

`general_name_matches` is how a distribution point's names are compared
against an IDP's (RFC 5280 §6.3.3(b)(1) "matches"). It exists because
`GeneralName`'s derived `PartialEq` is byte equality, which is wrong for
`directoryName`: DNs compare under RFC 4518 string prep.

## The survivors

    crl.rs:1584:9   delete match arm (GN::DirectoryName(a_dn), GN::DirectoryName(b_dn))
    crl.rs:1588:16  replace == with != in the `_ => a == b` arm

Deleting the DN arm drops to byte equality, so two DNs that differ only in
case or whitespace stop matching and a CRL that applies is refused -- a
fail-closed defect, and the arm's entire reason for existing.

`==` to `!=` on the other arm is the fail-open direction: non-DN variants
(`uniformResourceIdentifier`, `dNSName`) would match precisely when they
differ.

## What a test needs

A certificate whose `cRLDistributionPoints` names a distribution point, and a
CRL whose IDP names one too, in two forms:

  * both `directoryName`, DER-different but RFC 4518-equivalent (case) --
    kills the deleted arm;
  * both `uniformResourceIdentifier`, one pair equal and one pair different
    -- kills the `==` flip.

The PKITS vectors in `crl_dp_selection.rs` already drive the predicate and did
not kill either, so this wants its own fixture directory. The case-folded DN
trick is the one `ocsp-certid-binding/` uses.

## Found by

The first pkix-revocation mutation sweep, 2026-11-27.
close_reason: Both pinned. The directoryName arm needed a new fixture pair naming one DN in two cases (equal under RFC 4518, different as DER); the non-DN comparison turned out to be killed already by a_direct_crl_from_the_certificates_issuer_applies, added in 22114621 for the scope guards -- flip its == and two matching URI names stop intersecting. Commit for the DN arm follows 22114621.
